title: Builders Unbound
subtitle: Agents, amplified individuals and small teams
promise: Give more people the power to build what they need.
description: I am building for the next generation of builders: agents, solopreneurs and small teams turning expertise into products and companies. My bet is that more capable AI makes creation accessible to many more people. The tools that help me build, verify and grow can become products for other builders; their needs can improve my own system in return.
valueTest: A builder or authorized agent completes a useful task with less friction, better evidence or fewer interventions. Intended internal use is not verified adoption.
learnFrom: Time to a verified result, successful agent and human use, adopted improvements and repeat demand.
boundary: Building for agents does not require every product to have an API today. Interfaces and execution capabilities need their own acceptance evidence.

title: Main Street, Superpowered
subtitle: AI leverage for everyday businesses
promise: Make extraordinary capability useful in ordinary businesses.
description: I do not want AI leverage reserved for technology companies. Roofers, winemakers, bookkeepers and other domain experts should be able to put it to work without becoming software engineers. I build around a real job, a clear promise and a finished result—not AI added for its own sake.
valueTest: An everyday business accepts a useful deliverable or completes a workflow that improves how it operates or reaches customers.
learnFrom: Accepted outcomes, implementation friction, full delivery cost and repeat value.
boundary: A smaller team is not a reason to give the customer a smaller standard of care. Domain expertise, permissions and reliable delivery still matter.

title: Earn the Audience
subtitle: Distribution, trust and being chosen
promise: When more people can build, helping good work get chosen matters more.
description: My bet is that abundant software makes trusted distribution increasingly valuable. A useful product still has to be found, understood and chosen. I build ways to turn expertise into credible proof, useful content and relevant discovery—including search, AI answers and customer follow-through. Attention is the start of the job, not the outcome.
valueTest: The right person finds something useful and takes a meaningful next step, with measurable customer value behind the attention.
learnFrom: Qualified discovery, permissioned conversations, accepted work, repeat purchases and referrals.
boundary: Distribution is a strategic advantage, not literally the only moat. Product quality, reliability, relationships and defensible expertise still count. Spam is not distribution.

title: The Portfolio Advantage
subtitle: Multipreneurs, family offices and private equity
promise: Multiply the learning, not the overhead.
description: I expect AI leverage to make operating several businesses possible for more individuals and small teams. The same challenge already faces multipreneurs, family offices and private-equity operators: how does one business make the next better? I build for shared knowledge, clearer ownership decisions and reusable operating improvements—not a collection of disconnected dashboards.
valueTest: A portfolio operator makes a better-supported decision or reuses a verified improvement in another compatible business without multiplying routine work.
learnFrom: Decision usefulness, cross-business adoption, intervention load and durable economics by revenue family.
boundary: Several brands are not automatically several companies. Shared learning does not authorize shared customer data, and portfolio scale does not guarantee returns.

title: Healthspan, Not Hustle
subtitle: Health, capability and informed choices
promise: The point of more leverage is a life you are well enough to enjoy.
description: I want progress to buy back more than working hours. Health, energy and physical capability matter now—not only after a financial milestone. I build ways to understand health evidence, explore options and support useful everyday habits, keeping uncertainty and qualified clinical judgment in view.
valueTest: Someone finds a source-grounded answer, prepares better questions or completes a useful non-diagnostic next step.
learnFrom: Evidence quality, useful repeat engagement, safety-review outcomes and appropriate real-world follow-through.
boundary: Education and progress tools are not diagnosis, prescriptions or a promise of longer life. More confident language is not better evidence.

title: More Life, Less Admin
subtitle: Family, belonging, learning and everyday freedom
promise: Free up room for the things no machine should live for us.
description: Family dinners. Faith and purpose. Friendship and community. Learning something with your hands. An adventure that does not need to wait for a quieter quarter. These are ends worth building for. I explore products that make support easier to coordinate, meaningful things easier to preserve and everyday choices less exhausting.
valueTest: A person completes a useful activity, receives practical support, preserves something meaningful or makes a clearer everyday decision.
learnFrom: Completed value events, voluntary return use, trust and lower practical burden—not more time trapped in an app.
boundary: These are human priorities, not proof that the portfolio already serves every one of them. Connection and purpose are not outcomes I can manufacture for someone.
